architecture: Embedding → LSTM encoder → final (h,c) → LSTM decoder → Linear
strengths: simplest and smallest; fastest per step; good baseline
weaknesses: one fixed vector must store the whole message; forgets details of long inputs; cannot output OOV words

architecture: Embedding → BiLSTM encoder → bridge([h_fwd;h_bwd]) → LSTM decoder → Linear
strengths: each source word encoded with left and right context; cheap upgrade over A
weaknesses: still a single-vector bottleneck at the decoder; cannot output OOV words

architecture: Embedding → BiLSTM encoder → Bahdanau attention → LSTM decoder([x;context]) → Linear
strengths: reads the whole source at every step (no fixed bottleneck); interpretable attention weights
weaknesses: slower per step (attention over all source states); cannot output OOV words

architecture: BiLSTM + coverage attention + pointer/copy: P = p_gen·P_vocab + (1−p_gen)·Σ attention (extended vocabulary)
strengths: can copy source words, including words outside the vocabulary (IDs, rare numbers)
weaknesses: most parameters and slowest; copying can also reproduce source errors if p_gen is mis-calibrated
